name: pilot-v1-approximate
limitations: Pilot estimates, not a calibrated physical implementation. McPAT is an analytical model, not circuit simulation.
McPAT has separate integer/FP instruction windows; split the shared gem5 IQ equally, preserving its total capacity.
Use x86 micro-op counts for core activity; retain architectural instructions separately. gem5 integer/FP flags overlap, so partition by OpClass instead.

Scalar FU groups map to McPAT ALU/MUL/FPU equivalents. The SIMD FU group maps to scalar FPU equivalents, including integer SIMD activity; one issued SIMD operation counts as one scalar-equivalent access. Vector widths and FU multi-cycle switching are not calibrated.

CC register accesses fold into integer RF activity. CC, vector, predicate, matrix and misc register storage and the indirect branch predictor have no separate McPAT structures here. Integer/FP RF capacities alone come from gem5.
Rename writes use execution RF writes as a proxy for renamed destinations. CDB traffic uses issued arithmetic ops, including operations that may be squashed or have no register destination.

Ruby only exports combined cache demand hits/misses here. Split L1D activity in the executed load/store ratio. Split L2 in the aggregate L1 demand read/write ratio. Apply the same ratio to misses. Explicit fills/writebacks/coherence tag accesses are not fully represented.

Model L1 sharer metadata using McPAT merged_dir in each L2 bank. No separate full-memory directory SRAM is assumed; gem5 DirectoryMemory is an abstract functional structure. Additional directory/controller logic is not calibrated. Separate McPAT homenode activity fields retain its upstream one-event placeholders, rather than measured coherence traffic; directory activity is incomplete.

SimpleNetwork has no physical flits/VC buffers. Use a 128-bit equivalent router network, with one row of routers, actual port degree, three virtual networks and eight entries per VC. Count output-hop flits from message sizes; link geometry is McPAT's approximation, not the fully connected gem5 wiring layout.

Pipeline depth, x86 decoder/architectural register representation, cache ports/buffers and physical NoC choices are explicit model assumptions. Ruby TBEs are not directly interchangeable with McPAT MSHRs. McPAT unconditionally instantiates cache prefetch buffers, so a 16-entry proxy is included even though gem5 prefetching is disabled; zero entries cause CACTI to fail. Physical timing closure is not validated.
Memory-controller power uses McPAT's generic DDR controller approximation for DDR4. DRAM chips, board power and other peripherals are excluded.
Leakage is evaluated at the policy reference temperature with fixed Vdd; no temperature/leakage feedback or power gating. Use Runtime Dynamic, not Peak Dynamic, for ROI average power.
Cold-start effects are included in the full ROI, as specified by the experiment policy.
